name: shift
description:
The 'why now' argument: head centred, the question as a marine pull-quote band, the two scripts stacked in two thirds with the picture in the last third, and the close on the page's one full-strength accent moment.

The two scripts are NOT equal, and one rule per part branches on `data-script` — there were paired rules for every part because the view chose a different id per side: twenty-five selectors describing two things that differ in exactly two ways, the ground and the ink. The past script is a quiet annotation with its lines struck (the page's own strike-the-old gesture, third appearance); the future script wears the accent tint under a sunflower rule — sunflower measures 1.71:1 on cream and cannot be a glyph, but as a 3px rule it is a shape, the job it can hold.

The question sits on marine because it was drowning: cream type on cream ground, centred in its own row, read as a page that failed to load. The close is a sunflower FRAME, not a fill — solid across a block that size was shouting; marine on `accent-edge` measures 9.99:1.

base.$description: Hugging: the section unit's container is the box every cqi clamp in here measures, and a second container between them would change what they read.

inner.$description: One column, one left edge all the way down: the section mixed four measures and two alignments once, and the scripts read as a break rather than as its middle.

question.$description: A marine band, because the question was drowning: cream on cream, centred in its own row, its flex-item parens wrapping onto their own lines in three hundred pixels of nothing. The parens stay INLINE — inline cannot wrap onto its own line the way a flex item can — and on marine they are a shape and a tone rather than the 3.93:1 they have to justify on cream.

spread.$description: Two thirds argument, one third picture. The scripts stack — the old above the new, the order a reader moves through them — and the close spans BOTH tracks: it is the section's last word and belongs to the whole spread, not one column of it.

scripts.$description: The rule-label's index comes from the DOM position, not a parameter — `ruleLabel(text, '01')` was the view numbering itself; the counter numbers them from where they sit.

& .shift-script-items > li > span:last-c.$description: Struck, like the salary and like 'working to survive': the script being left behind, said without a word of copy.

&[data-script='with'].$description: Warm ground, warm ink: marine on this tint is 13.01:1 and correct, but it made the panel a blue island in a yellow field; `accent-foreground` is the ramp's own ink at 10.67:1, so the diptych differs in BOTH ground and ink rather than ground alone.

turn.$description: A FRAME, not a fill: solid sunflower across a block this size was the loudest thing on the page. The tone belongs on the edge, where it still says 'this is the accent moment', with the ground a step lighter behind the type. Used once on the page, at the moment there is something to decide — the only way an accent stays an accent.

a11y.note: The heading keeps its id as the section's `aria-labelledby` target. The struck items carry their meaning in copy as well as in the strike; the script counters render through `::before` on the rule-label, so the numbering a reader hears matches the DOM order it is derived from.
